label: input token o at one of the first three original positions (t<3)
explanation: Fires only when the input token is o and it sits at original position 0, 1 or 2. Precision is 1.0 and recall is about 0.998 on dev. Magnitude depends on position: about 0.95-1.0 of max at t=0 and t=1 (the max, 2.32, is reached at t=1 after s), and about 0.55-0.6 at t=2. It does not fire on o at original positions 3 and later, on any other token, or on the delimiter. In the copy phase it fires only on a few very weak traces (<0.1 of max) when o is fed back. Sequence length, repeated tokens and previous tokens have little effect apart from the position effect.

issues: Minor: there are 13 dev-split activations on o at original position 3, all very weak (for example 0.03 of max), so 'does not fire on o at positions 3 and later' is true in practice but not strictly.

The test-split misses (99) are all weak copy-phase traces (0.02-0.12 of max) where o is fed back, mostly at step 5 in L=3 sequences. That matches the explanation and holds about 0% of the activation mass. There are no false positives.
The magnitude claim fits the mass shares. t=0, 1 and 2 have similar active counts (about 16.7k each) but mass shares of 0.386, 0.389 and 0.226, which puts t=2 at about 0.58 of the t=0/1 level.
